title: A randomized trial of intensive versus standard blood-pressure control
authors: SPRINT Research Group, Wright JT Jr, Williamson JD, Whelton PK, Snyder JK, Sink KM, et al.
followUp: median 3.26 years; intervention stopped early for benefit
population: Adults with systolic blood pressure of 130 mm Hg or higher and increased cardiovascular risk, without diabetes
funder: NIH contracts and an inter-agency agreement (National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute; National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases; National Institute on Aging; National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke); Clinical and Translational Science Awards at several sites; resources and facilities of the Department of Veterans Affairs. NIH scientists participated in the design and held one vote on the steering committee; the coordinating centre analysed the data.
inKindSupport: Azilsartan and azilsartan combined with chlorthalidone were donated by Takeda Pharmaceuticals International and Arbor Pharmaceuticals; neither company had any other role in the study.
result: Primary outcome in 243 of 4678 (5.2%; 1.65% per year) with a systolic target below 120 mm Hg versus 319 of 4683 (6.8%; 2.19% per year) with a target below 140 mm Hg (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.89); number needed to treat 61 during the median 3.26 years. Serious adverse events possibly or definitely related to the intervention in 220 (4.7%) versus 118 (2.5%) (HR 1.88).
